title: SMB Signing Not Required

references.name: MITRE ATT&CK - T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay

description: Hosts that do not require SMB signing are vulnerable to adversary-in-the-middle and NTLM relay attacks. An attacker positioned on the network (often via LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning) can relay captured SMB authentication to other hosts that also lack signing, authenticating as the victim and potentially executing commands.
businessImpact: High --- relayed authentication can grant access to file shares or administrative access to other systems, enabling lateral movement and data compromise.
remediation:
- Require SMB signing on all servers and clients via Group Policy.
- Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS to reduce authentication-poisoning opportunities.
- Disable SMBv1 entirely.
- Restrict and segment SMB traffic, and enforce the use of authenticated, signed protocols.
